title: Featurizing Full Medical History for Modelling
text: We have the history of when which ICD codes were assigned to each patient, so we can featurize this time series to get the following sets of values per patient.

title: Featurizing Full Medical History for Modelling
section: Describe Basic Feature of Medical History
text:
Describe Basic Feature of Medical History
Here the “history” is every time they were assigned a unique ICD code on a specific date, so a 2-column tibble with the columns encounter_date and ICD_code. We can compute the “cumulative” ICD code set at each point in time, either total codes assigned or total unique codes assigned. So with this cumulative code counts (total or unique) we can compute several features per patient “summarizing” their history.

history_metric: wheter metric is calculated with total or unique code counts
n_codes: number of codes assigned over total history
n_visits: number of unique visits
history_length: medical history length in real-time (days)
mean_codes_per_visit: n_codes / n_visits
code_frequency: n_codes / history_length
normalized_mean_time: see linked notes below
KS_vs_uniform: see linked notes below
shannon_entropy: see linked notes below
burstiness: see linked notes below

There are some more basic features like “length”, “total nunber of codes” etc. which can calibrate our “confidence”/data richness per patient and more “shape-like” features that have richer interpretations, see further notes here

Now we can plot the “basic” features and the more “complex” features


Code
all_medical_history_shape_features_df %>%
    pivot_longer(
        -c(FID, history_metric),
        names_to='history_shape_feature',
        values_to='value'
    ) %>%  
    # filter(history_shape_feature %notin% c('mean_codes_per_visit')) %>% 
    mutate(
        complexity=
            case_when(
                history_shape_feature %in% 
                    c(
                        'normalized_mean_time',
                        'KS_vs_uniform',
                        'shannon_entropy',
                        'burstiness'
                    ) ~ 'complex',
                .default='basic'
            )
    ) %>% 
    {
        ggplot(
            data=.,
            mapping=
                aes(
                    x=history_shape_feature,
                    y=value
                )
        ) +
        # geom_boxplot(aes(fill=history_metric)) +
        # ggh4x::facet_nested(
        #     # history_shape_feature ~ history_metric + complexity,
        #     complexity ~ history_metric,
        #     scales = 'free'
        # ) +
        ggh4x::facet_nested(
            rows = vars(history_metric), 
            cols = vars(complexity, history_shape_feature),
            scales = 'free',
            independent = 'y',
            strip = 
                ggh4x::strip_nested(
                    by_layer_x = TRUE,
                    text_x = 
                        list(
                            ggplot2::element_text(),  # outer
                            ggplot2::element_blank()  # inner
                        )
                )
        ) +
        make_ggtheme() +
        theme(
            legend.position='top',
            axis.title=element_blank(),
            axis.text.x=element_text(angle=45, hjust=1, vjust=1)
        )
    }

title: BSR 1715 Final Project
text:
For this project we examine the Mt. Sinai Millions Cohort, investigating patients experiences with Suicidal Ideation and/or Actions. Here are the steps in our analysis for clean + investigating + interpreting the data:

Patient Demographics & Outcomes
Featurizing Medical History Per Patient
Linear Modelling
Bootstrapping

title: Patient Demographics and Outcomes
text: The dataset is for patients part of the Mt. Sinai Millions (MSM) cohort, for each patient we have some demographic information and their “medical history”. The medical history is the list of ICD codes (specifiyng diagnoses) assigned to a patient by a doctor during a hospital visit for all recorded vists for that patient. So for every visit recorded we have the set of ICD codes assigned. We will turn this long-form medical history into a set of descriptive features for each patient that are better suited to linear modelling where patients are independent data points. We also use the medical history to define the outcome we are studying for each patient and whether they experience SI, Broad SA or Narrow SA.

Plot individual distributions for all 40280 patients with no missing data.


Code
make_single_ggbar <- function(col_name, plot_df=demographics_df){
    plot_df %>% 
    select(!!sym(col_name)) %>%
    count(!!sym(col_name)) %>% 
    add_column(feature=col_name) %>%  # dummy x-axis
    mutate(pct=prop.table(n)) %>%  # counts to percentages
    arrange(!!sym(col_name)) %>% 
    mutate(ypos=1 - (cumsum(pct) - pct/2)) %>%  # percentage label position on figure
    {
        ggplot(
            data=.,
            aes(
                x=feature,
                y=pct,
                fill=.data[[col_name]],
            )
        ) + 
        geom_col(position='stack') +  # stacked bar plot
        geom_text(
            aes(
                label=scales::percent(pct, accuracy=0.1),
                y=ypos
            ),
            vjust=0.5,    # nudge above top of bar
            size = 3
        ) + 
        scale_y_continuous(labels=scales::percent) +
        guides(fill=guide_legend(ncol=1)) +
        make_ggtheme() +
        theme(
            legend.position='right',
            axis.title=element_blank()
        )
    }
}

title: Patient Demographics and Outcomes
text:
Defining Patient Outcomes
For every patinent we want to create a discrete output column that specifies what experience (if any) the patient had with Suicidal Ideation or Actions. We have 3 lists of ICD codes, where for each list a patient is a “case” if they were assigned a matching code >= 1 time, and control otherwise. These “directly” observed outcomes are:

Ideation (SI)
Broad Action (Broad SA)
Narrow Action (Narrow SA)
Substance Use Disorder (Substance UD)
Alcohol Use Disorder (Alcohol UD)

We can further define outcomes based on combinations of SI, BSA and NSA. Each of these combinations excludes some set of samples to make the case/control comparison more clearly interpretable.

Code
direct_outcomes <- unique(load_ICD_Phenotype_Mappings()$outcome.type)
# all_patient_outcomes_df
all_patient_outcomes_df %>% 
    select(FID, outcome.type, case_control_status) %>%
    mutate(outcome.definition=ifelse(outcome.type %in% direct_outcomes, 'direct', 'inferred')) %>% 
    group_by(
        outcome.definition,
        outcome.type,
        case_control_status
    ) %>% 
    summarize(n=n()) %>%
    mutate(pct=prop.table(n)) %>%  # counts to percentages
    mutate(ypos=1 - (cumsum(pct) - pct/2)) %>%  # percentage label position on figure
    {
        ggplot(
            data=.,
            mapping=
                aes(
                    x=outcome.type,
                    y=pct
                )
        ) + 
        geom_col(aes(fill=case_control_status), position='stack') +  # stacked bar plot
        geom_text(
            aes(
                y=ypos,
                label=
                    scales::number(
                        n,
                        accuracy=0.1,
                        scale_cut=scales::cut_short_scale()
                    ),
            ),
            vjust=0.5,    # nudge above top of bar
            size = 3
        ) + 
        facet_grid(
            cols=vars(outcome.definition),
            # rows=vars(metric),
            scales='free'
        ) +
        scale_y_continuous(labels=scales::percent) +
        make_ggtheme() +
        theme(
            axis.text.x=element_text(angle=45, hjust=1, vjust=1),
            axis.title=element_blank(),
            legend.title=element_blank()
        )
    }

title: Linear Modelling across different Outcomes
text:
Parameter Comparisons
Most basic thing, run a glm with all features and look at betas + p-values + variance contributions for each model. Basically just summary(glm(outcome ~ demographics + has_alcohol_UD + has_substance_UD + history_features))
